reproduction.baseline_false_green: Installed CLI accepted put --data '{"value":NaN}' with exit 0 and persisted NaN in organon.json; MCP status then returned text containing nan with no structured result.
current_negative_controls: CLI rejects NaN, Infinity in nested data, 1e9999, nonzero numbers such as 1e-9999 that would underflow to zero, and 0.1234567890123456789 because its decimal value would change on round-trip serialization; rejected inputs leave the ledger unchanged.
CLI --roles, --expected-deps and run manifest reject nonfinite JSON.
Python ledger append rejects nested nonfinite values before atomic replacement.
Reading a contaminated ledger through the real MCP client fails instead of reporting a successful status; a direct ledger test rejects an underflow literal on read.
reproduction.current_positive_control: Valid Unicode and finite decimal data retain CLI/MCP structured status parity; 0.1, 1.00, 1e20 and explicit signed zero forms remain accepted.

limits: This guards JSON syntax and the decimal value seen after float parsing and JSON round-trip serialization; binary floating-point still does not represent ordinary decimals exactly in memory. Evidence requiring exact decimal arithmetic needs an explicit representation or an independently reviewed tolerance.
The MCP client can serialize a nonfinite outgoing Python value to null before the server sees it; the poisoned-ledger test checks server-side reading, not that client serialization path.
The clean smoke covers its synthetic routes and does not establish every possible production state or GOAL criterion 1.
